messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: realtime-latency-detector triggered: p95 and p99 above SLO for /v1/generate in us-west-2 for the last 3m. Pager severity: P1 :rotating_light:

sre_oncall_zoe: seeing it on my phone, switching to laptop. joining.

runtime_lead_jorge: on it, looking at the grafana panel (https://grafana.redwood/team/realtime/p95p99). p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~520ms; p99 to ~2.1s. spike started ~1711239600.

infra_oncall_amy: current cluster utilization looks normal overall but one GPU pool (dedicated-gpu-3) shows high queue depth. scaling events? not yet.

prod_support_micah: any customer-facing errors? Support reported one user complaining about slow chat responses ~5m ago (ticket #45218).

ml_runtime_dev_ben: could be KV cache misses on long-tail sessions — we rolled kv-cache TTL change yesterday in canary. checking rollout status.

runtime_lead_jorge: good call. can you check per-route KV hit ratio? query: `SELECT route, kv_hit, kv_miss FROM telemetry.realtime WHERE ts > 1711239500 LIMIT 50` — paste results?

ml_runtime_dev_ben: quick dump: `/v1/generate` kv_hit=61% kv_miss=39% (baseline 90/10). streaming endpoints kv_hit down to 42%.

sre_oncall_zoe: streaming tail latency panels show piles of stalled streams — many with `stall_detected=true`. p99 stall duration median ~950ms. logs show backpressure: `client_write_timeout` spikes.

infra_oncall_amy: I can bump capacity for dedicated-gpu-3 and enable burst pool. doing `infra scale pool dedicated-gpu-3 --replicas +2` now. ETA ~90s.

incident-bot: NOTE: autoscaling triggered for dedicated-gpu-3 10m ago but suppressed due to burst policy set to manual.

runtime_lead_jorge: that's... not ideal. Investigate why autoscaler suppressed. amy, can you temporarily allow burst? otherwise we'll route traffic to other pools.

infra_oncall_amy: enabling burst now: `infra set-burst-policy dedicated-gpu-3 --enabled true` — done.

sre_oncall_zoe: rerouting suggestion: temporarily shift 30% of /v1/generate traffic to fallback model rdx-small-latency-optimized via routing rule. low-risk, preserves outputs for most users.

ml_runtime_dev_ben: rdx-small has slightly lower quality but significantly lower tail latency. I'll open a canary rule: `router add-rule --route /v1/generate --percent 30 --model rdx-small-latency-optimized` — applying.

runtime_lead_jorge: adding the canary. monitor p95/p99 in next 2 minutes.

sre_oncall_zoe: quick health checks: curl to /v1/generate test prompt returned in 180ms against fallback, 1.8s against primary.

prod_support_micah: posting an internal status update to customers now: "We are seeing elevated latency for some real-time requests in us-west-2. We're mitigating and will update in 15 minutes." :phone:

incident-bot: ACTION LOG: route adjustment initiated by ml_runtime_dev_ben at 1711239950.

infra_oncall_amy: scale completed, new replicas active. queue depth dropping on dedicated-gpu-3.

sre_oncall_zoe: metrics trending downward after both scale and route shift. p95 dropped to ~220ms, p99 to ~630ms. still above SLO but improving.

runtime_lead_jorge: suspect root cause: KV cache miss spike due to TTL rollback combined with partial autoscaler suppression -> transient queueing + streaming stalls. Need full rollback/patch.

ml_runtime_dev_ben: confirming canary of kv-cache TTL change was rolled to 40% last night; I see a config flip on 1711239300 that set default_ttl=10s by mistake. rolling that back to 300s now. `config set kv.default_ttl 300 --env prod --range us-west-2`.

sre_oncall_zoe: please post the runbook link for tail latency investigation. we should also collect a sample of stalled stream traces: `ddtrace.query("service:runtime AND trace_id:*-stall*")`.

runtime_lead_jorge: runbook: https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/latency-tail-investigation. key steps: check kv hit ratio, check k8s pod restarts, inspect queue depth, check model fallback rates.

ml_runtime_dev_ben: rollback applied at 1711240120. KV hit ratio climbing back to baseline. streaming kv_hit now ~85%.

sre_oncall_zoe: great. follow-up: confirm no ongoing customer-impacting errors. micah, any new tickets?

prod_support_micah: only the original slow-response ticket; updated them with mitigation and ETA. will keep monitoring.

infra_oncall_amy: on autoscaler suppression: found a stale policy in the dedicated pool config that required manual approval for burst after last maintenance. removing that constraint and creating a ticket to fix the policy template: INC-17261.

runtime_lead_jorge: good. action items: (1) revert kv TTL config fully and run canary audits, (2) fix autoscaler policy template, (3) add a temporary alert for kv_hit_ratio <80% for streaming routes.

sre_oncall_zoe: handoff: I'm documenting the incident and will keep the channel open for 20 minutes post-resolution. If anything resurges, page the oncall as P1.

ml_runtime_dev_ben: will follow up with a config postmortem and PR link once merged.

prod_support_micah: updating status to customers: "Latency reduced; mitigation in place; root cause identified as a misconfigured KV TTL rollout. Full fix underway." :white_check_mark:

sre_oncall_zoe: marking incident as mitigated at 1711240445. leaving channel open for final checks.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: p95/p99 returned within SLO at 1711240449. Summary: misconfigured kv-cache TTL + suppressed autoscaler led to queueing and streaming stalls; mitigations: scale up pool, enable burst, route 30% to low-latency fallback, rollback TTL change. Postmortem assigned to ml_runtime_dev_ben, infra_oncall_amy.
